FOXP2 was of particular interest among those genes, given that it encodes a transcription factor mutated in developmental verbal dyspraxia ( 39 , 40 ), and is implicated in a number of neuropsychiatric disorders.
Yet, we also observed a previously unknown enrichment of FOXP2 expression in L3–5 intratelencephalic excitatory neurons across primates, that was not detected in mice ( Fig. 6A ).
This analysis also highlighted human L3–5 intratelencephalic subclass enrichment of PKD2L1 , which encodes a calcium-regulated cation channel.
